Katanga Mining Ltd Announces Major Expansion in DRC Copper Operations

Katanga Mining Ltd has unveiled plans for a significant expansion of its copper extraction operations in the Lualaba province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), aiming to boost annual production capacity by 25% over the next three years. The announcement was made on Thursday at a press conference held at the company’s Kolwezi site, where local officials and industry representatives gathered to hear details of the ambitious project.

“This investment underscores our long-term commitment to the region and to the development of the Congolese mining sector,” said Jean-Marc Mutombo, Katanga Mining Ltd’s regional director. “With demand for copper rising globally, particularly for use in renewable energy technologies, we are confident that this expansion will create new opportunities for economic growth and job creation here in Lualaba.”

The company stated that the expansion will involve the construction of new processing facilities and the deployment of advanced ore extraction technologies. According to preliminary estimates, the project will require an investment of approximately $180 million and is expected to create more than 600 direct jobs during the construction phase, with additional positions opening once the facilities become operational.

Local authorities welcomed the announcement, emphasizing the potential benefits for the community. “This project will not only increase tax revenues for our province, but also support local businesses and infrastructure,” said Lualaba Governor Henri Tshiswaka. “We look forward to working closely with Katanga Mining Ltd to ensure the expansion is conducted responsibly and sustainably.”

Industry analysts say the move strengthens the DRC’s position as a leading global copper producer. “Katanga’s investment signals renewed confidence in Congolese mining and should attract further interest from international investors,” observed mining analyst Pauline Kabemba of Kinshasa-based consultancy Cobalt Strategies.

Construction is slated to begin in September, pending final regulatory approval. Katanga Mining Ltd has pledged to prioritize local hiring and community engagement throughout the process.
